title: The Rendlesham Forest Incident
hook: In 1980, US airmen chased strange lights through an English forest at night.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: Airmen at a Royal Air Force base saw lights descend into the nearby woods.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Patrolling the forest, they reported a glowing object, and later found three marks on the ground.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Radiation readings at the site were reportedly higher than the normal background level.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: Deputy base commander Charles Halt wrote an official memo describing the event.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: Some suggest a lighthouse beam or bright meteor caused the confusion that night.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: Many of the airmen involved still insist what they saw was not of this world.

end.line: What really landed in Rendlesham Forest?

description: In December 1980, US airmen at an English airbase reported lights and a strange craft in nearby Rendlesham Forest. It remains Britain's most famous unexplained military encounter.

facts.claim: In late December 1980, US Air Force personnel at RAF Woodbridge and Bentwaters in Suffolk, England, reported strange lights in the nearby Rendlesham Forest.
Patrols investigating the forest reported finding marks on the ground, along with reports of elevated radiation readings at the site.
Deputy base commander Lt Col Charles Halt wrote an official memo to the UK Ministry of Defence describing the events.
facts.source: Wikipedia: Rendlesham Forest incident; Halt memo

facts.claim: Some investigators have proposed the lights were a nearby lighthouse beam or a bright meteor, combined with unfamiliarity among the witnesses.
It is widely considered the most famous UFO case connected to the British military.
Several of the airmen involved have maintained in later interviews that they still believe what they saw was not conventional.
